chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Hasan ibn Jahm, from Abu Al-Yaqzan, from Ubaydullah ibn Al-Walid, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'There are three (things) with which nothing will harm [a person]: Supplication during distress, seeking forgiveness during sin, and gratitude during blessings.'
ai.seo_question: What are the three things that protect a believer from harm according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this concise tradition from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), highlighting a triad of spiritual remedies that neutralize divine affliction. This teaching underscores the dynamic relationship between human action and divine response, where gratitude preserves blessings, repentance removes guilt, and supplication in distress invokes mercy, reflecting the Shia emphasis on practical spirituality (amal) as a means of maintaining spiritual equilibrium.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Hasan Bin Jahm, from Abu Al Yaqzan, from Ubeydullah Bin Al Waleed who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘There are three (things), nothing would harm along with these – The supplication during the worries, and the seeking of Forgiveness during the sin, and the gratefulness during the Favours’.
en.sarwar: 7. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from Hassan ibn Jahm from abu al-Yaqdan from ‘Ubayd Allah ibn al- Walid who has said the following: “

I heard abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) saying, ‘With the existence of three factors nothing can harm one. These factors include: prayer in difficulties, asking forgiveness in sins and thankfulness for bounties.’”
